cap: Type I endometrioid carcinoma follows a long estrogen-driven road: unopposed estrogen causes hyperplasia, cytologic atypia marks the step to endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia, and PTEN loss and mismatch repair defects appear early, so tumors are usually low grade and found early through postmenopausal bleeding. Type II serous carcinoma arises in the atrophic endometrium of older women through an early TP53 mutation and is high grade from the start.
